title: Batch Config Playbook — Personal mini-tracker
body:
Purpose: quick personal tracker for micro-experiments that tune batch size, kv-prefix caching and light quant options. Not meant for canonical results — capture trends and weird tails.

CSV table (run summary) -- columns: run_id, date, model, quant, batch_size, seq_len, kv_prefix_cached, throughput_tok_s, p50_ms, p95_ms, cost_per_1k_tokens_usd, notes

run-001,2025-01-16,redwood-7b-v1,none,1,64,false,210,38,95,0.032,baseline single-request (no batching)
run-002,2025-01-16,redwood-7b-v1,none,4,64,false,720,95,270,0.012,good throughput gain; p95 grows sublinearly
run-003,2025-01-17,redwood-7b-v1,8-bit,4,64,false,900,110,300,0.009,quant helps throughput, slight p95 increase
run-004,2025-01-18,redwood-7b-v1,8-bit,8,128,true,1800,145,420,0.007,cached prefix + bigger batch = best token/s but p95 up
run-005,2025-01-20,redwood-7b-v1,4-bit,8,128,true,1600,160,520,0.006,4-bit instability on long seqs (spikes at p95)
run-006,2025-01-22,redwood-7b-short,none,16,32,true,2800,60,190,0.005,short model + large batch yields low p50, solid p95
run-007,2025-01-24,redwood-13b-v1,8-bit,4,64,false,420,65,350,0.025,13b heavier baseline, consider auto-fallback plan
run-008,2025-02-05,redwood-7b-v1,8-bit,12,64,true,1950,130,480,0.006,throughput saturated, p95 jitter from GC-like pauses
run-009,2025-02-10,redwood-7b-v1,none,2,512,true,540,210,920,0.020,long seqs blow up latency even with cache
run-010,2025-02-18,redwood-7b-v1,8-bit,6,256,true,1200,180,610,0.010,middle ground for long sequences

Quick observations:
- Batching improves tokens/sec predictably, but p95 increases nonlinearly after a threshold (observed ~8-12 batch depending on seq).
- KV-prefix caching reduces work for repeated prefixes (chat warmup) — big win for short-turn dialogue flows.
- 8-bit quantization gives good throughput gains with acceptable p50; watch p95 on long sequences (memory/compute stalls).
- 4-bit aggressive quant has occasional instability on tail latencies: mark as "needs more runs".
- For long seq_len (>256) prioritise smaller batch sizes and prefer short-model variants when semantics allow.

Cheap cost calc snippets (back-of-envelope):
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd column estimated from instance cost and measured throughput; rough formula I used: instance_hour_cost / (throughput_tok_s * 3600) * 1000.
- Example: instance_hour_cost=0.80 USD, throughput=1800 tok/s -> cost = 0.80 / (1800*3600) * 1000 ≈ 0.000123 \* my sheet numbers include rounded amortized infra overhead -> final 0.006 in table).

Open questions / hypotheses to validate:
- Are p95 spikes correlated with specific kernel selection paths? (need trace + kernel logs)
- Does increasing batch_size beyond 12 lead to queueing backpressure at the API gateway? (monitor request queue length)
- Can we auto-suggest batch settings per route based on observed seq_len distribution? (proto: per-route heuristic in front of router)

Quick todo (me):
- [ ] Push trace capture for run-008 and run-010 (capture kernel-level timings and GC).
- [ ] Add a column for 'cpu_util' and 'gpu_mem_free' next round.
- [ ] Try mixed strategy: small leader batch for latency-sensitive traffic + periodic large-batch background jobs.
- [ ] Link experiment to PR that added kv-cache metrics (GITHUB:infra/serving-runtime PR#482)

Notes-to-self: keep this light. When results look promising, port table to shared Confluence and open a short note for product about 'recommended default route configs' for chat vs long completion use-cases.

References & quick links:
- Confluence playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Batching-Playbook
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime -> thread ts 1673802000 (search 'batch p95 spike')
- GitHub PRs: infra/serving-runtime PR#482 (kv-cache metrics), infra/optim PR#371 (quant rollout)

Last quick raw log excerpt (for context):
- 2025-02-05 14:33 run-008 saw 3 p95 spikes within 10 minutes, correlated with new driver kernel version v2.3.4. Suspicious.

End of sheet. Keep small, keep iterating.
